request.deadline: 9-month delivery period from July 2026 to March 2027
deliverables: Audited Bitcoin-Cardano bridge running on Cardano mainnet under controlled access
Federated and SPO threshold custody modes
Open-source smart contracts, off-chain tooling, and SDK
Reporting on operations, milestones, treasury disbursements, and on-chain activity
request.what: Phase 1 funding to take Bifrost from working testnet to launch readiness, including hardening, security audits, formal verification, ecosystem and partner readiness, stewardship, and economic foundations.

claims.claim: Bifrost is designed as a permissionless Bitcoin-Cardano bridge secured by Cardano's SPO ecosystem that brings BTC onto Cardano as native fBTC.
The proposal requests ₳12,332,031, including a 10% refundable contingency, for Phase 1 work by FluidTokens and Lantr Engineering.
Bifrost is already live on testnet under Catalyst Fund 14, with working peg-ins and peg-outs and participating SPOs.
By the end of Phase 1, Bifrost will be an audited bridge running on Cardano mainnet in both federated and SPO threshold custody modes under controlled access.
The proposer states that custody of locked BTC is distributed across 400+ Cardano SPOs weighted by delegation, requiring a threshold representing a majority of delegated stake.
The proposer states Bifrost will have no bridge token, no founder allocation, and no built-in ongoing revenue claim for the founding teams.
Bifrost smart contracts, off-chain tooling, and SDK are said to be released under Apache 2.0 for audit, forking, operation, and permissionless integration.
The proposal targets 1,200 BTC, about 600,000 annual transactions, and 3,000 fBTC-holding wallets by Q2 2029.
The proposer claims bridge fee surplus will be split to SPOs and the Cardano Treasury in fBTC.
The document says public rollout and 24 months of operations are intentionally deferred to a Phase 2 proposal in Q1 2027.

summary: The document presents a large Phase 1 treasury request for a Bitcoin-Cardano bridge, with concrete requested amount, timeframe, and intended deliverables, but most security, adoption, open-source, and economic-sustainability claims are proposer assertions within the supplied text rather than independently evidenced there.
